column1: # Every statement the site makes about U-Vision, its status, and where this repository backs it.
# Not published: it sits outside public/ and the build never reads it. test/claims.test.ts matches its ids against
# the claim ids in src/ (both ways), checks that every ref exists, and that the page marks exactly the vision rows
# as roadmap. Change a sentence, change its row in the same commit.
# status: works = works today · design = how it is built (a principle or a boundary) · vision = a goal, not built yet · promise = an operating commitment
# ref: one or more repository paths, joined with " · ". A vision row points at the roadmap section of README.md.

column4: context
Still-triggered capture, judged by the server's vision model against scenario criteria and reference images, with defect type and finding; browser app
Criteria written per scenario as text and OK/NG reference images
Every decision stored with its image, finding and confidence, filed by date; with a dedicated model, each judge's answer is recorded in a decision ledger
Human-confirmed results become training data; the dedicated model takes over by authority stages
On-device motion detection, blur rejection before upload, manual shutter
NG split into the defect types a scenario declares, with a finding
VLM unavailable means "unable to decide", never an automatic OK
Expected part number, match/mismatch, code read on the device compared first
Device-first capture queue, sent oldest first on reconnect, judged once (Idempotency-Key), capture time stored
Results by date and scenario, a review-only view; the review list holds only disagreements or low-confidence items; human OK/NG labels
Day summary with counts by defect type; CSV download
Training readiness signal from human-confirmed labels per class; rule-selected dataset export through the API
Optional ML classifier alongside the VLM; disagreements go to the review list
Four authority stages, starting with the dedicated model recorded only (run in parallel); promotion by admin, automatic demotion
Confirmed-case memory judging similar items without training (roadmap)
Fixed-camera video scenarios, including early fire and smoke warning (roadmap)
Edge device processing video, sending events and crops, buffering offline (roadmap)
Line-crossing counting against the work order plan (roadmap)
Hard-hat watch with duration-based alerts, no face judgment (roadmap)
Anomaly detection from normal images only, explained by the VLM (roadmap)
OpenAPI document, signed CloudEvents webhooks
Work orders, lots and expected part numbers taken in from the MES (roadmap)
MQTT and OPC UA output (roadmap)
Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model server (GPUStack provider)
File system storage, no database server
Installation on a server inside the customer's company and maintenance by iyulab; runs as its own application and connects to other systems over the network

Adoption path: one scenario, one tablet run alongside the current inspection with human checks, measured from the record (defect catch rate and false-alarm rate; no promotion signal on too few confirmed cases), judgment handed over as far as the measurements support
No accuracy claim; human labels and metrics for on-site measurement
Single organization, open operator screen, admin PIN for changes
This site sets no cookies and loads no tracking scripts
